proof:
There are finitely many nonempty compact convex sampled fibers $K_z$. Each has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine dimension $r_z$, since it contains a full relative simplex and lies in a bounded relative ball. Hence $q=\max_z r_z$, and $0<\mathcal H^q(S)<\infty$ is the sum of the measures of the $q$-dimensional fibers. The lower-dimensional fibers are $\mathcal H^q$-null.

Take $C_\varepsilon=C+(\{0\}^n\times\varepsilon B_d)$, which remains a convex body. Its integer base set is exactly the old one, and its fiber at each such base is $K_z+\varepsilon B_d$, of positive $d$-volume. Write $\nu_\varepsilon$ for the raw mixed volume on the thickened trace. The Euclidean tube limit in each affine fiber, together with the extra factor $\varepsilon^{q-r_z}$ for $r_z<q$, gives
$$
\varepsilon^{-(d-q)}\nu_\varepsilon\rightharpoonup
\kappa_{d-q}\mathcal H^q|_S.
$$
The fibers are finitely many, their embeddings in the ambient space are isometric, and the same scaling gives convergence of the total masses to $\kappa_{d-q}\mathcal H^q(S)>0$. Thus the normalized measures $\mu_\varepsilon$ converge weakly to the normalized intrinsic measure $\mu$.

Choose $\varepsilon_k\downarrow0$ and points $y_k$ of depth at least $c$ in the thickened traces by the premise. They lie in a common compact set and within distance $\varepsilon_k$ of $S$ in their own fibers. A convergent subsequence therefore tends to $y\in S$. Fix any closed halfspace $H=\{w:a\cdot w\ge b\}$ containing $y$. For every $\delta>0$, the fixed enlarged halfspace $H_\delta=\{w:a\cdot w\ge b-\delta\}$ contains all sufficiently late $y_k$ on the subsequence. Portmanteau for this closed set gives
$$
\mu(H_\delta)\ge\limsup_k \mu_{\varepsilon_k}(H_\delta)\ge c.
$$
Continuity from above as $\delta\downarrow0$ gives $\mu(H)\ge c$, including any mass on the original boundary. The convergent subsequence was chosen before the arbitrary $H$, so the same $y$ works for every containing closed halfspace. The zero-block cases follow from the stated dimension conventions.

statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$ and $c\in[0,1]$. Assume that every convex body $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ whose integer trace has positive mixed $d$-volume has a point of normalized closed-halfspace depth at least $c$ for that mixed volume. Let $C$ be any convex body with nonempty integer trace $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ and let $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S$. Then $S$ has a point of closed-halfspace depth at least $c$ for the normalized intrinsic measure $\mathcal H^q|_S/\mathcal H^q(S)$, including $q=0$. The case $n=0$ already has $q=d$ for a convex body, and when $d=0$ the measure is counting measure throughout.
title: A conditional lossless transfer from full mixed volume to intrinsic depth
